report_name: Surge in Cyberattacks Observed Against Taiwanese (.tw) Websites

threat_actors.name: Unidentified Scanning Actor Targeting Taiwan
threat_actors.description: An unidentified threat actor operating a large-scale reconnaissance campaign originating from the IP address 45.38.60.254, specifically targeting Taiwanese websites with vulnerability scans for SQL injection and malicious file uploads.

attack_patterns.name: Vulnerability Scanning
attack_patterns.description: The threat actor used automated tools to systematically scan a large number of Taiwanese (.tw) websites for specific, known vulnerabilities, primarily SQL Injection and Malicious File Upload flaws.

attack_patterns.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
attack_patterns.description: The goal of the scanning campaign was to identify exploitable SQL Injection and Malicious File Upload vulnerabilities in public-facing web applications, such as WordPress and its plugins, to gain initial access.

campaigns.name: October 2026 .tw Domain Scanning Campaign
campaigns.description: A large-scale, targeted reconnaissance campaign starting in late October 2026, characterized by a tripling in attack volume against Taiwanese (.tw) websites. The campaign focused on scanning for web application vulnerabilities.

identities.name: Taiwanese Websites
identities.description: Websites using the .tw country-code top-level domain, particularly WordPress sites, were targeted by a large-scale reconnaissance campaign involving vulnerability scanning.

infrastructure.name: Scanning Infrastructure 45.38.60.254
infrastructure.description: A single IP address (45.38.60.254) identified as the source of over 246,000 blocked attack requests targeting Taiwanese websites with vulnerability scans.

indicators.name: Potential SQL Injection Web Scanning Attempt
indicators.pattern:
title: Potential SQL Injection Web Scanning Attempt
id: 8c3d4e5f-6a7b-4891-8cde-f12345678901
status: experimental
description: Detects web requests containing common SQL injection patterns in the URI, consistent with reconnaissance activity observed targeting Taiwanese websites in late 2026.
references:
  - https://www.wordfence.com/blog/2026/11/45-38-60-254-the-scanner-behind-the-november-2026-rise-in-attacks-on-tw-websites/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-20
tags:
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.initial_access
level: medium
logsource:
  category: proxy
detection:
  selection_1:
    c-uri|contains|all:
      - 'SELECT '
      - ' FROM '
  selection_2:
    c-uri|contains:
      - ' UNION SELECT '
  condition: 1 of selection_*
indicators.description: Detects web requests containing URI patterns indicative of SQL injection attempts, such as those used in the scanning campaign against Taiwanese websites.

indicators.name: Potential WordPress Malicious File Upload Attempt
indicators.pattern:
title: Potential WordPress Malicious File Upload Attempt
id: 9d4e5f6a-7b8c-4012-8def-123456789012
status: experimental
description: Detects web requests attempting to exploit malicious file upload vulnerabilities, particularly targeting WordPress sites as seen in a campaign against Taiwanese domains in late 2026.
references:
  - https://www.wordfence.com/blog/2026/11/45-38-60-254-the-scanner-behind-the-november-2026-rise-in-attacks-on-tw-websites/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-20
tags:
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.initial_access
level: medium
logsource:
  category: proxy
detection:
  selection_post:
    cs-method: 'POST'
  selection_path:
    c-uri|contains:
      - '/wp-admin/admin-ajax.php'
      - '/wp-content/plugins/'
      - 'upload.php'
  condition: all of selection_*
indicators.description: Detects POST requests to common WordPress paths associated with file upload vulnerabilities, a key vector in the scanning campaign against Taiwanese websites.
